title: Vanishing of higher cohomology on affines
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module. For any affine open $U\subset X$ we have
$\mathrm H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p>0$.
(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.2.2, Tag
[01XB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XB).*)

proof.text: Regard the affine open U as the induced open subscheme U of X. Its structure sheaf is the restriction of the structure sheaf of X, and the restriction of the quasi-coherent module F to U is quasi-coherent. The hypothesis that U is affine gives an affine scheme in the sense of the affine-scheme vanishing theorem.

source.place: node pqf-lem-affine-vanishing, reduction from an affine open to its induced affine scheme

proof.text: Apply the affine-scheme vanishing theorem to the induced affine scheme U and the restricted quasi-coherent module F|_U. It gives Subsingleton ((F|_U).H (q + 1)) for every natural q, equivalently H^p(U,F|_U)=0 for every p>0.

source.place: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.2.2, Tag 01XB

proof.text: Cohomology of the induced open subscheme U with the restricted module is, by the definition of restriction to an open subscheme and of the cohomology notation in the statement, the displayed group H^p(U,F). Therefore the vanishing obtained in Step 2 is exactly the conclusion for every p>0.
